title: Baron Hirsch founds an association that settles persecuted Jews from Russia as farmers in Argentina

trailer.text: Baron Maurice de Hirsch, a German-Jewish financier and philanthropist, set up charitable foundations to promote Jewish education and improve the lot of oppressed European Jewry.
According to the Christian Science Monitor, the Jews in Russia needed a refuge from the pogroms that began in 1881.
According to the Posen Library, in 1891 Hirsch founded the Jewish Colonization Association to facilitate mass Jewish emigration from Europe and Russia to rural Argentina.
Moisés Ville, the largest of the colonies, had four synagogues, three Yiddish newspapers, two Yiddish libraries and a Jewish theater.
The organization is still active in Israel, under the name Jewish Charitable Association.

paragraphs.text: According to the Christian Science Monitor, the Jews in Russia needed a refuge from the pogroms.
The pogroms began in 1881, after the assassination of Czar Alexander II.
According to Zablotsky, the pogroms of 1881/82 struck the south of the empire, about 200 within one year.
According to Zablotsky, the territory in which Jews were legally allowed to live was reduced by 90%.
According to the 1897 census, of 5,215,805 Jews, 94% lived in the Pale of Settlement.
In 1891, Jews still living in Moscow and St. Petersburg were forced to sell their property in haste and leave.

stations.title: The man, and the son he lost

paragraphs.text: Maurice de Hirsch was a German-Jewish financier and philanthropist.
For generations, the Hirsch family occupied a prominent position in the German-Jewish community.
He was born in Munich in December 1831.
According to Zablotsky, shortly after the death of his only son, Lucien, Hirsch decided to retire from business.
In a letter replying to condolences, Hirsch wrote that he had lost his son but not his heir, for humanity is his heir.
After Lucien's death, the Baron conceived the idea of creating foundations to raise the moral and material status of the Jews of Eastern Europe.
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, Baron Maurice de Hirsch was born in Munich on December 9, 1831.
Hirsch offered the Russian government a fund for the education of the Jews in the Pale of Settlement.
The fund's statutes were submitted to the government, which was at first favorably disposed but soon changed its attitude.
The government was willing to accept the money but refused to allow a foreigner to be involved in its administration.
According to Norman, Hirsch's response was to attempt to move large numbers of Jews out of Russia and establish them as farmers in a free country.
In 1889, Dr. Löwenthal, returning from a trip to Argentina, suggested to him founding a colony in that country.
On 20 August 1890, a conference was held at the Baron's residence in Paris.
A commission sent to Argentina submitted a favorable report six months later.
Even before the Association, in 1889, Russian Jews arrived in Buenos Aires aboard the ship Weser.
According to Norman, at Palacios station, in conditions of neglect, 50–60 children died.
According to Zablotsky, a typhus epidemic killed 60 children there.
Hirsch wrote that after careful examination he had become convinced that Argentina, Canada and Australia offered the surest guarantee for the plan, and that he would begin in Argentina.
According to Zablotsky, Argentina seemed suitable because of its size, sparse population, climate and fertile land.
In August 1891, Hirsch wrote that he would try to make for the Jews a new home in different lands, where they would be free farmers on their own soil.
According to HaMichlol, he saw settlement in Argentina as a solution to antisemitism and as a territory for establishing a Jewish state.
In July 1891, Hirsch wrote that he was decidedly opposed to the old system of alms-giving.
In his words, the greatest problem in philanthropy is to make human beings capable of work out of those who would otherwise become beggars, and so to create useful members of society.
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, the Association was founded by the Baron in September 1891 and incorporated in London.

According to Article 3 of its statutes, its purpose was to assist and promote the emigration of Jews from Europe or Asia, principally from countries in which they were subjected to special taxes or restrictions.
Hirsch subscribed for almost all of the shares himself.
In August 1891, by his direction, some 3,000 square leagues of land were purchased in Argentina, for $1,300,000.
At first, two tracts were allocated for settlement: Mauricio in the province of Buenos Aires and Moisés Ville in the province of Santa Fe.
Moisés Ville was founded by Russian immigrants even before the Association.
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, Moisés Ville was founded by Russian immigrants in 1890, before the association was established, and the association reorganized it in 1891.
Colonists began to arrive in the summer of 1891, and by the end of the year they numbered 2,850.
Moisés Ville, the largest of the colonies, had four synagogues, three Yiddish newspapers, two Yiddish libraries and a Jewish theater.
According to HaMichlol, by Hirsch's death his enterprise had brought about 10,000 Jews to Argentina, and about two-thirds of them were absorbed in the colonies.
Over the years, the younger generation left the colonies for the big cities, mainly Buenos Aires.
According to an article in the Christian Science Monitor, at the time of its writing about 250,000 Jews lived in Argentina, the largest Jewish population in Latin America.
In February 1891, the Baron Hirsch Fund was established in the United States, with an endowment of 2.4 million dollars, later increased to 4 million.
In response to an appeal from the Jewish community of Montreal, Hirsch sent a cheque for $20,000.
In July 1893, he sent 200,000 marks to a group of Jewish refugees stranded in Libau.
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, the Association aided about 20,000 persons in emigrating from Romania.
By the end of 1902, the Association's loan banks in Galicia had 3,912 shareholders.
In 1895, Hirsch met Herzl in Paris, and they discussed the settlement of Jews in Argentina.

According to the Christian Science Monitor, Herzl proposed that Hirsch finance immigration to Uganda, then a British colony in Africa, but Hirsch disagreed and believed that Argentina offered a more secure future. The article does not state when the proposal was made.
Hirsch disagreed, believing that Argentina offered a more secure future.
Hirsch died on 21 April 1896 at Ógyalla in Hungary.
According to HaMichlol, with his death the idea of a Jewish state in Argentina was abandoned, but Jews continued to emigrate there.
The 1929 Encyclopaedia Britannica described the Association as probably the greatest charitable trust in the world.
In Thessaloniki, Hirsch is commemorated in the names of a commercial stoa, a street and a district in the city center.
The organization is still active in Israel, under the name Jewish Charitable Association.

A. D. Goldhaft, a student at the Baron de Hirsch Agricultural School in Woodbine, New Jersey, wrote that his life was positively affected by Hirsch's work, even though most of the settlements did not last.
Zablotsky argues that in a social evaluation that takes the external effect into account, one could conclude that the project was highly successful.

According to Zablotsky, only 2,500 immigrants were actually relocated in the first year, one tenth of the target of 25,000 planned for 1892. However, according to the same source, this target may have served only as a basis for negotiations with the Russian government, and Hirsch himself spoke in an 1891 interview of a thousand immigrants in the first year.
The historian Dubnow wrote that it was clear the mountain had given birth to a mouse.
The colonists lost their crops through locusts, rains, drought and inexperience.
They suffered droughts, storms, floods and locusts that destroyed crops within hours.
About 800 less satisfied colonists were deported to the United States within about two years.
In October 1893, 2,683 persons remained in the colonies.

claims.text: לפי המכלול, עד מות הירש הביא מפעלו לארגנטינה כ-10,000 יהודים, כשני שלישים מהם נקלטו במושבות.
claims.quote: עד שנה זו הצליח מפעלו של הברון להביא לארגנטינה כ-10,000 יהודים, וכשני שלישים מהם נקלטו במושבות

claims.text: עם השנים עזבו בני הדור הצעיר את המושבות לערים הגדולות, בעיקר בואנוס איירס.
claims.quote: במרוצת השנים עזבו בני הדור הצעיר את החיים הקשים במושבות המרוחקות לטובת מגורים בערים הגדולות, בעיקר בואנוס איירס

claims.text: כיום חיים בארגנטינה כ-250,000 יהודים, האוכלוסייה היהודית הגדולה ביותר באמריקה הלטינית.
claims.quote: Today, Argentina has about 250,000 Jews, the largest population in Latin America.

claims.text: בפברואר 1891 הוקמה קרן הברון הירש בארצות הברית, בהון של 2.4 מיליון דולר שהוגדל מאוחר יותר ל-4 מיליון.
claims.quote: with the establishing of the Baron Hirsch Fund, with an endowment of 2.4 million dollars, later increased to 4 million.

claims.text: בתגובה לפנייה מהקהילה היהודית במונטריאול שלח הירש המחאה על 20,000 דולר.
claims.quote: but for the present was enclosing a cheque for $20,000

claims.text: ביולי 1893 שלח הירש 200,000 מרק לקבוצת פליטים יהודים שנתקעה בליבאו.
claims.quote: without delay the Baron sent a draft for 200,000 marks to the Libau group

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית, החברה סייעה בהגירתם של כ-20,000 איש מרומניה.
claims.quote: It has aided about 20,000 persons in leaving Rumania

claims.text: עד סוף 1902 היו לבנקי ההלוואות של החברה בגליציה 3,912 בעלי מניות.
claims.quote: By the end of 1902 these banks had altogether 3,912 shareholders with 7,929 shares of 10 kronen each

claims.text: ב-1895 נפגש הירש עם הרצל בפריז ודנו ביישוב יהודים בארגנטינה.
claims.quote: בשנת 1895 נפגש הברון הירש עם בנימין זאב הרצל בפריז, והשניים דנו ביישוב היהודים בארגנטינה.

claims.text: לפי ה-Christian Science Monitor, הרצל הציע שהירש ימן הגירה לאוגנדה, אך הירש לא הסכים וסבר שארגנטינה מציעה עתיד בטוח יותר.
claims.quote: Theodore Herzl, the founder of modern Zionism, proposed that Hirsch finance immigration to the then-British African colony of Uganda. But Hirsch disagreed

claims.text: הירש מת ב-21 באפריל 1896 באוגיאלה שבהונגריה.
claims.quote: Hirsch died at Ógyalla in Hungary (now Hurbanovo, part of Slovakia) on 21 April 1896.

claims.text: עם מות הירש באפריל 1896 נזנח הרעיון של מדינה יהודית בארגנטינה, אך יהודים המשיכו להגר אליה.
claims.quote: עם מותו של הירש באפריל 1896 נזנח רעיון הקמת המדינה היהודית בארגנטינה, אך יהודים המשיכו להגר לארגנטינה

claims.text: האנציקלופדיה בריטניקה מ-1929 תיארה את החברה כנאמנות הצדקה הגדולה ביותר בעולם כנראה.
claims.quote: The 14th edition of the Encyclopaedia Britannica, published in 1929, still referred to JCA as probably the greatest charitable trust in the world.

claims.text: בסלוניקי הונצח הירש בשם סטואה מסחרית, רחוב ושכונה במרכז העיר.
claims.quote: Hirsch is honoured also with naming a commercial stoa, a street and a district at the center of Thessaloniki, Greece.

claims.text: א.ד. גולדהפט, תלמיד בית הספר החקלאי בווּדבריין, כתב שחייו הושפעו לטובה מעבודת הירש גם אם רוב ההתיישבויות לא החזיקו מעמד.
claims.quote: Perhaps some of the settlements that he set up failed to have a spectacular success, and most of them failed in time, but my life was helped by his work

claims.text: זבלוצקי טוען שבהערכה חברתית שמביאה בחשבון את ההשפעה החיצונית ניתן להסיק שהפרויקט הצליח מאוד.
claims.quote: si se realizara la evaluación social del proyecto, tomando en cuenta la externalidad generada por el mismo, podría concluirse que el proyecto fue altamente exitoso

claims.text: בפועל הועברו בשנה הראשונה רק 2,500 מהגרים, עשירית מהמתוכנן.
claims.quote: tan sólo 2,500 inmigrantes, un décimo del número proyectado, fueron reubicados durante el primer año

claims.text: דובנוב כתב שהיה ברור כי ההר ילד עכבר.
claims.quote: Unos pocos años después resultaba claro que la montaña había dado vida a un ratón.

claims.text: המתיישבים איבדו את יבוליהם בגלל ארבה, גשמים, בצורת וחוסר ניסיון.
claims.quote: The colonists were subjected to many trials, losing all their crops through locusts, heavy rains, drought, and their own inexperience.

claims.text: המהגרים סבלו מבצורות, סופות, שיטפונות וארבה שהשמיד יבולים תוך שעות.
claims.quote: The immigrants suffered periodic droughts, dust and rain storms, floods, and locust swarms that wiped out crops in a matter of hours.

claims.text: המתיישבים נתקלו בתנאי אקלים קשים ובאסונות טבע שהשמידו יבולים.
claims.quote: המתיישבים היהודים נתקלו בקשיים רבים, אשר כללו תנאי אקלים קשים בהם לא היו מורגלים, אסונות טבע שהשמידו את היבולים

claims.text: כ-800 מתיישבים מרוצים פחות גורשו לארצות הברית בתוך כשנתיים, ובאוקטובר 1893 נותרו 2,683 נפש.
claims.quote: it was necessary to deport so many discontented colonists to the United States—800 were deported within about two years—that in October, 1893, only 2,683 persons remained

claims.text: לפי עדותו של דוד פיינברג, הירש איבד את בנו היחיד ב-1889.
claims.quote: En 1889, el difunto Barón de Hirsch perdió a su único hijo, un joven en quien el padre y la madre habían puesto grandes esperanzas.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית, עם מות הירש הגיע קרן החברה ל-6,000,000 לירות.
claims.quote: Through the death of Baron de Hirsch the Jewish Colonization Association came into possession of a fund amounting to £6,000,000 ($30,000,000).

claims.text: לפי ויקיפדיה, הירש יסד את החברה בהון של 2,000,000 לירות והעניק לה ב-1892 עוד 7,000,000 לירות.
claims.quote: with a capital of £2,000,000, and in 1892 he presented to it a further sum of £7,000,000.

claims.text: לפי זבלוצקי, ההון ההתחלתי של החברה היה 10,000,000 דולר, כולו מהירש, שהוסיף עליו 30,000,000 דולר.
claims.quote: dotada de un capital inicial de U$S 10,000,000, constituido en su totalidad por el Barón de Hirsch, quien luego lo habría de incrementar en U$S 30,000,000

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית, נרכשו בסך הכול למעלה מ-17,000,000 אקר.
claims.quote: In all, over 17,000,000 acres were acquired. At first the project of settling Russian refugees on a large scale in Argentina met with a protest from the government

claims.text: לפי זבלוצקי, סך הקרקעות שרכשה החברה הגיע ל-620,000 הקטר.
claims.quote: el total de los terrenos adquiridos por la J.C.A. alcanzaría las 620,000 hectáreas

claims.text: לפי ספריית פוזן, עד 1930 רכשה החברה למעלה מחמישים אלף הקטר בארגנטינה, ויותר מעשרים אלף מתיישבים יהודים חיו ועבדו בהם.
claims.quote: By 1930, the JCA had purchased over fifty thousand hectares of Argentinean farmland where more than twenty thousand Jewish colonists lived and worked.

claims.text: לפי ה-Christian Science Monitor, בין 1891 ל-1932 קנתה החברה למעלה מ-1.5 מיליון אקר עבור 9,011 מהגרים.
claims.quote: Between 1891 and 1932, the JCA bought over 1.5 million acres for 9,011 immigrants, according to author Ricardo Feierstein

claims.text: לפי זבלוצקי, המושבות בארגנטינה מעולם לא עברו 27,500 תושבים.
claims.quote: las colonias en nuestro país nunca llegaron a tener mas de 27,500 habitantes

claims.text: לפי אלקין, מספר התושבים הגיע ל-33,000.
claims.quote: Según J. Elkin (1998), dicho número ascendería a 33,000 habitantes.

claims.text: לפי ספריית פוזן, עד 1930 חיו ועבדו בארגנטינה יותר מעשרים אלף מתיישבים יהודים.
claims.quote: more than twenty thousand Jewish colonists lived and worked

claims.text: לפי ווינסברג, התוכנית המקורית הייתה להעביר לארגנטינה 25,000 יהודים רוסים ב-1892.
claims.quote: El proyecto original de la J.C.A. consistía en trasladar a la Argentina 25,000 judíos rusos durante 1892

claims.text: בראיון ב-1891 אמר הירש שבשנה הראשונה ישלח אלף איש, בשנייה אלפיים, בשלישית שלושת אלפים, עד עשרת אלפים.
claims.quote: The first year we will send one thousand, the next year two thousand, and the third three thousand, and so on up to ten thousand.

claims.text: ב-1891 הגיעו לקונסטנטינופול 900 יהודים רוסים שרצו להתיישב בפלשתינה.
claims.quote: In 1891, 900 Russian Jews intending to settle in Palestine arrived in Constantinople.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית, הברון מוריס דה הירש נולד במינכן ב-9 בדצמבר 1831.
claims.quote: born at Munich Dec. 9, 1831

quote_translations.c80: Baron Hirsch saw Jewish settlement in Argentina as a solution to the antisemitism experienced by the Jews of Eastern Europe, and as a territory in which the Jews could establish a Jewish state.
quote_translations.c46: And the first of the Jewish colonies was Moisés Ville, which was founded in 1889 (even before Baron Hirsch's support)
quote_translations.c57: By this year the Baron's enterprise had succeeded in bringing about 10,000 Jews to Argentina, and about two-thirds of them were absorbed in the colonies
quote_translations.c61: Over the years, the younger generation left the hard life in the remote colonies in favor of living in the big cities, mainly Buenos Aires
quote_translations.c69: In 1895 Baron Hirsch met Binyamin Ze'ev Herzl in Paris, and the two discussed the settlement of the Jews in Argentina.
quote_translations.c71: With Hirsch's death in April 1896 the idea of establishing the Jewish state in Argentina was abandoned, but Jews continued to emigrate to Argentina
quote_translations.c79: The Jewish settlers encountered many difficulties, which included harsh climatic conditions to which they were not accustomed, natural disasters that destroyed the crops
